column1: # fe-timed-events.tsv -- SE's 2006 TIMED EVENTS, served on a schedule (world/timedevents.py).
# SE ran each of these ONCE, in 2006, as a patch-day switch with an end time (polnews,
# the archived www.playonline.com/fe pages). Repeating them EVERY YEAR on the same dates
# is OURS. The times are the ones SE's notices give, JST: an event began when that day's
# version-up finished and ended at the time the notice names.
# One row per (event, effect); the rows of one event share its `event` id and show on
# the admin Calendar as one entry. Columns are read by name, any order:
# event    the event's id (lower case, no spaces)
# name     its English name (OURS where SE gave none); name_jp = SE's own, kept as data
# tag      the word the server log prints when the effect applies (blank = the name)
# start, end  'MM-DD HH:MM' JST, every year; an end before the start wraps over New Year
# effect   drop_rate   monster drop rates x value (fe-drops.tsv rows; items = only those)
#          kill_exp    monster kill EXP x value
#          war_exp     war result EXP x value (the one-level-per-war cap still holds)
#          dragon_feast  the Dragon summon for BOTH armies from the war's start, no
#                      losing-side rule, value = per-army cap; items = the item it needs
#                      (blank = feunit's --summon-items DRAGON=)
#          shop_sale   every shop's buy prices x value (gold and Rings; items = only those)
#          quest       a limited-time quest: NOT SERVED (it needs the event VM's quest
#                      conversation, which is not built). Recorded so the history is here.
# value    the multiplier, or the cap for dragon_feast
# items    optional comma list of item numbers (see effect)
# served   1 = the server applies it, 0 = recorded only (not on the Calendar either)
# source   SE's notice; note = free text
# news     what players read in the news and on Discord (the event's first row
#          that has one); blank = the Calendar's own description
# announce 0 = served but kept out of the news (an event not yet seen working on
#          a console); blank or 1 = announced
# A row with a bad time, an unknown effect or a bad number is refused and logged.
# --timed-events off turns the whole table off; a path names another file.
